mainTopic: Finishing the כהן גדול's שחיטה, and אביי's order of the daily עבודה with the גמרא's sources for each link
overview: This עמוד opens at the end of the discussion of the כהן גדול's שחיטה on יום כיפור. The גמרא confirms that cutting most of the סימנים is fully valid, with not even a rabbinic פסול. Another כהן still finishes the cut, because completing it is a מצוה. Then אביי lays out, from received tradition and following אבא שאול, the full order of the daily services in the מקדש. His list runs from the morning wood piles to the afternoon תמיד, and it closes with the פסוק 'עליה השלם כל הקרבנות כולן'. The גמרא then goes through the list item by item to find a source or reason for each one. A ברייתא and סברא show that the big pile comes before the קטורת pile. The double 'עליה' shows that the קטורת pile comes before the two logs. Three answers (רבי ירמיה, רבינא, רב אשי) defend why the logs come before cleaning the inner מזבח. For why the inner מזבח comes before the lamps, אביי admits he knows it only by tradition, while רבא cites ריש לקיש's rule 'אין מעבירין על המצות', which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Cutting the majority is fully valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer. The משנה repeats 'רוב אחד בעוף ורוב שנים בבהמה' to teach that cutting the majority of the סימנים is completely valid, with not even a rabbinic פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why we learned: the majority of one sign in a bird, and the majority of two signs in an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up its previous answer. It explains why the משנה bothered to say that cutting 'most' of the סימנים is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that a שחיטה of the majority of each סימן is not just valid after the fact. There is not even a rabbinic problem with it. This sets up the next question: if cutting most is fully fine, why does another כהן need to finish the cut?

keyTerms.meaning: That is why we learned (this teaching)
Majority (most of the סימן)
Bird (needs only one סימן cut)
Animal (needs both סימנים cut)

phrases.english: Therefore, we learned:
the majority of one sign in a bird
and the majority of two signs in an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun on the previous עמוד, before This amud starts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why a משנה repeats a teaching
steps.terutzMaskana: Cutting the majority of the סימנים is fully valid, with no rabbinic invalidation.

steps.title: Why finish the cut at all?
steps.stepSummary: If cutting the majority has no flaw at all, even rabbinically, why does the משנה require another כהן to finish the cut?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since there is not even a rabbinic invalidation, why do I need to finish the cut?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the procedure in the משנה. If the כהן גדול's partial cut is already perfect, the finishing seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge builds directly on step 1. If cutting most is fully valid, then having a second כהן finish the cut looks unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what the finishing adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (introduces a premise)
An invalidation by rabbinic law
To finish or complete (the cut)

phrases.english: And since
there is not even an invalidation by rabbinic law,
why do I need to finish the cut?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 1 to question the משנה's procedure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement that another כהן finish the cut
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the partial cut is completely valid, finishing it seems to serve no purpose.

steps.title: Finishing the cut is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Even though cutting the majority is valid, it is a מצוה to complete the cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a מצוה to finish the cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that finishing is not needed for validity. It is still a מצוה to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates two questions: whether the שחיטה is valid, and what the best way to do it is. The שחיטה is valid without finishing. Completing the cut is still the preferred מצוה, for example so that the blood flows out fully.

keyTerms.meaning: A preferred מצוה, not required for validity

steps.whatToRemember: Cutting most of the סימנים is fully valid. Another כהן still finishes the cut because completing it is a מצוה.

phrases.english: It is a מצוה to finish the cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates validity from the preferred מצוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Finishing the cut seemed to have no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: Finishing is not needed for validity, but it is a מצוה to do it.

steps.title: אביי's order: the morning preparations
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins listing the order of the daily services, based on tradition and following אבא שאול. The list opens with the wood arrangements, the cleaning of the inner מזבח, and five of the מנורה's lamps.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי laid out the order based on tradition, following אבא שאול. The large wood pile comes before the second pile for the קטורת. The second pile comes before placing the two logs. Placing the two logs comes before cleaning the inner מזבח. Cleaning the inner מזבח comes before cleaning five lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new section starts here. אביי begins a long list of which daily service in the מקדש comes before which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's list rests on a received tradition (גמרא), not on new reasoning, and it follows אבא שאול's view. The first items are preparations. First the wood piles on the outer מזבח are set up. Then the inner מזבח is cleaned of ashes, and then five lamps of the מנורה are cleaned.

keyTerms.meaning: Laid out the order (of the services)
Based on received tradition
The large wood pile on the outer מזבח, where offerings are burned
Two logs of wood added on top of the large pile
Removing ashes
Cleaning and preparing the lamps of the מנורה

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word מערכה is used in two ways. In 'מסדר מערכה' it means the order of services. In 'מערכה גדולה' it means a pile of wood on the מזבח.

phrases.english: Abaye arranged the order of the services
based on tradition
and in accordance with Abba Shaul:
the large arrangement of wood precedes
the second arrangement, for the incense;
the second arrangement for the incense precedes
setting up the two logs of wood;
and setting up the two logs of wood precedes
removing the ashes from the inner altar;
and removing the ashes from the inner altar precedes
cleaning five lamps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the שחיטה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order: large wood pile, then second pile for the קטורת, then two logs, then cleaning the inner מזבח, then cleaning five lamps.

steps.title: אביי's order: from the תמיד's blood to the נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The list continues with the blood of the morning תמיד, the last two lamps, the קטורת, the limbs, the מנחה, the חביתין, and the נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cleaning five lamps comes before the blood of the תמיד. The blood comes before cleaning two lamps. Cleaning two lamps comes before the קטורת. The קטורת comes before the limbs. The limbs come before the מנחה, the מנחה before the חביתין, and the חביתין before the נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues the same list. It now moves into the main morning offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cleaning of the מנורה is split in two. Five lamps are cleaned before the blood of the morning תמיד, and the last two are cleaned after it. Next comes the קטורת inside, and then the burning of the תמיד's limbs and its accompanying offerings. The verb 'קודם' (precedes) is dropped partway through, but the meaning stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood of the morning daily offering (slaughtered and sprinkled)
Incense burned on the inner מזבח
The limbs of the תמיד, burned on the outer מזבח
The כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering
Wine libations

phrases.english: And cleaning five lamps precedes
the blood of the daily offering;
the blood of the daily offering precedes
cleaning two lamps;
and cleaning two lamps precedes the incense;
the incense precedes the limbs;
the limbs precede the meal-offering;
the meal-offering precedes the griddle-cakes;
and the griddle-cakes precede the libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲטָבַת חָמֵשׁ נֵרוֹת קוֹדֵם לְדַם הַתָּמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list directly from the last item in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order: five lamps, then the blood of the תמיד, then two lamps, then קטורת, then limbs, then מנחה, then חביתין, then נסכים.

steps.title: אביי's order: ending with the afternoon תמיד
steps.stepSummary: The list ends: נסכים, then מוספין, then the בזיכין, and finally the תמיד של בין הערבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The libations come before the additional offerings. The additional offerings come before the frankincense bowls. The bowls come before the afternoon daily offering.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes the list. The afternoon תמיד is the very last offering of the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra offerings come after all the regular morning services. These are the מוספין on special days and the בזיכין of frankincense on שבת. The afternoon תמיד closes the day, and the next step gives the source for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Additional offerings on שבת, ראש חודש, and יום טוב
Bowls of frankincense offered on שבת with the לחם הפנים
The afternoon daily offering

phrases.english: And the libations precede the additional offerings;
and the additional offerings precede the frankincense bowls;
and the bowls precede the afternoon daily offering,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list begun in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נסכים, then מוספין, then בזיכין, then the afternoon תמיד, which comes last.

steps.title: Verse source: all offerings are completed upon the morning עולה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים' is read as 'complete all the offerings on it.' So all other offerings come after the morning תמיד and before the afternoon תמיד, which ends the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And he shall burn on it the fats of the peace-offerings.' The word 'on it' means: complete all the offerings on it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי's list ends with a פסוק that supports its last item: the afternoon תמיד must come after everything else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עליה' refers to the morning עולה. The דרשה reads it as 'השלם': complete all offerings on top of the morning תמיד. That means every other offering belongs between the two תמידים, so the afternoon תמיד is always last.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is stated (introduces a פסוק)
'On it', referring to the morning עולה
Complete (a wordplay on שלמים)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי following אבא שאול, the daily order runs from the wood piles in the morning to the afternoon תמיד, which is always last. The source is 'עליה — השלם כל הקרבנות כולן.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that nothing is offered after the afternoon תמיד, frames the whole daily schedule in the מקדש. It will matter as the סוגיא goes on to discuss the order of the services.

phrases.english: as it is stated:
"And he shall burn on it the fats of the peace-offerings";
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from ויקרא ו:ה.

phrases.english: "on it": complete
all of the offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural support for ending the list with the afternoon תמיד.
steps.raayaObject: That all offerings are completed before the afternoon תמיד, which comes last
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא ו:ה, 'והקטיר עליה חלבי השלמים', read as 'עליה השלם'

steps.title: What is the source that the big wood pile comes first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first item in אביי's list and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: the big wood arrangement comes before the second arrangement for the קטורת. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first item in אביי's list and asks for a source. This line sets up the next step, which brings the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the order is based on tradition, but the גמרא wants to know if a פסוק supports each item. This question opens a long section that checks the list one item at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: The big wood pile on the outer מזבח, where the קרבנות are burned
The second, smaller wood pile. Its coals are taken inside to burn the קטורת.
'From where do we know this?' A request for a source

phrases.english: The Master said:
The large arrangement precedes
the second arrangement for incense.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מַעֲרָכָה גְּדוֹלָה קוֹדֶמֶת לְמַעֲרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁל קְטוֹרֶת. מְנָא לַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first item in אביי's list (Step 4) to find its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the מערכה גדולה is set up before the מערכה שניה של קטורת.

steps.title: A ברייתא reads the two halves of one פסוק as the two piles
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the first half of the פסוק refers to the big pile and the second half to the קטורת pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'It is the עולה on its fire-place on the מזבח all night' refers to the big pile. 'And the fire of the מזבח shall burn on it' refers to the second pile for the קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that splits one פסוק into two parts. The first part refers to the big pile and the second part to the קטורת pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the big pile first, so we learn that the big pile comes first in the order. The words 'fire of the מזבח' are read as a second, separate fire, which is the קטורת pile.

keyTerms.meaning: Its burning place, the fire on the מזבח
Shall be kept burning on it

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
"It is the burnt-offering on its fire-place
upon the altar all night" —
this is the large arrangement.
"And the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it" —
this is the second arrangement for incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק first mentions the עולה's fire, which is the big pile, and then 'the fire of the מזבח,' which is the קטורת pile. So the big pile comes first.

steps.title: Why not reverse the two readings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first half of the פסוק could not refer to the קטורת pile instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I could reverse them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Maybe the first half of the פסוק means the קטורת pile and the second half means the big pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself does not say which half matches which pile. If the readings were switched, the order would flip and the קטורת pile would come first. The proof only works if we can show why the first half must be the big pile.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And I could reverse it.' This challenges an assignment by suggesting the opposite.

phrases.english: And I could reverse them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the way the ברייתא in Step 9 assigns each half of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the first half of the פסוק refers to the מערכה גדולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the wording forces this assignment. Switching the two readings would reverse the order.

steps.title: The big pile matters more because it brings more כפרה
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense to give the big pile first place because many קרבנות are burned on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical that the big pile is more important, because its כפרה is greater.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with logic. The more important pile should be the one mentioned first, and the big pile is more important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the קרבנות are burned on the big pile, while the second pile serves only the קטורת. Since the big pile brings much more כפרה, it should be the one matched to the first half of the פסוק and done first.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical, it makes sense
Is preferable, is more important
Its כפרה is greater, because many קרבנות are burned on it

phrases.english: It is reasonable that the large arrangement is preferable,
since its atonement is extensive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reason (סברא) for preferring one reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two readings of the פסוק could be swapped.
steps.terutzMaskana: The big pile is more important, so it gets the first half of the פסוק and comes first.

steps.title: The קטורת pile has a special importance of its own
steps.stepSummary: The opposite argument: the second pile is more important because its coals are taken inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, the second pile is more important, because coals from it are brought inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The second pile also has something special about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coals from the קטורת pile are carried into the היכל to burn the קטורת on the inner מזבח. The big pile is used only outside. That could make the second pile seem more important, which would weaken the answer in Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On the contrary.' This argues for the opposite conclusion.
Coals from it are brought inside, into the היכל

phrases.english: On the contrary, the second arrangement is preferable,
since they bring coals from it inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the מערכה גדולה is more important.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second pile is used inside the היכל, which is a competing kind of importance.

steps.title: Greater כפרה still outweighs being used inside
steps.stepSummary: Even so, the greater כפרה of the big pile is the stronger reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the fact that its כפרה is greater is more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both reasons are real, but greater כפרה is the stronger one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not deny that the second pile is used inside. It weighs the two reasons and decides that bringing more כפרה wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so

phrases.english: Even so,
its extensive atonement is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing two reasons against each other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being used inside might make the second pile more important.
steps.terutzMaskana: Greater כפרה is the stronger reason, so the big pile comes first.

steps.title: A second answer: the big pile can replace the small one
steps.stepSummary: If there is no wood for the second pile, coals are taken from the big pile. So the big pile is the main one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you like, say: if one does not find wood for the second pile, wouldn't he bring coals in from the big pile?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the challenge in Step 12. The second pile is not truly independent, because the big pile can take its place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the coals for the inside קטורת can come from the big pile when needed. So the second pile is only an extra, and it adds nothing the big pile cannot do. That makes the big pile the main one, and it comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say.' This introduces a second, different answer.
Brings in

steps.whatToRemember: The מערכה גדולה comes before the קטורת pile for two reasons. It brings more כפרה, and it can serve both purposes, while the second pile is only an extra.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא מַשְׁכַּח עֵצִים לְמַעֲרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה,
phrases.english: if one does not find wood for the second arrangement,
would he not bring coals in from the large arrangement?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the challenge in Step 12, alongside Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Takes away the special importance of the second pile
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because its coals go inside, the second pile has an importance the big pile lacks.
steps.terutzMaskana: The big pile can also supply coals for inside, so it is the main pile and comes first.

steps.title: What is the source that the קטורת pile comes before the two logs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next item in אביי's list and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second pile for the קטורת comes before arranging the two logs. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in אביי's list and asks for a source. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'two logs' are the extra logs added to the fire each morning. The גמרא wants a source showing that the second pile is already set up by the time these logs are added.

keyTerms.meaning: Arranging the two logs of wood added to the מזבח fire

phrases.english: The second arrangement for incense
precedes the arranging of the two logs of wood.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁל קְטוֹרֶת קוֹדֶמֶת לְסִידּוּר שְׁנֵי גְּזִירֵי עֵצִים. מְנָא לַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in אביי's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the מערכה שניה is set up before the two logs.

steps.title: 'Upon it' and not upon the other pile, so the other pile already exists
steps.stepSummary: The word 'עליה' excludes the other pile, which shows that the other pile is already there when the logs are added.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the כהן shall burn wood upon it every morning.' 'Upon it,' and not upon the other pile. This shows that the other pile already exists.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק about adding wood each morning. It points out that the word 'עליה' is there to exclude the other pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah only needs to say 'upon it and not the other' if the other pile is already on the מזבח when the logs are added. So the second pile must be set up before the two logs.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall burn, meaning add wood to the fire
Its companion, the other pile
'By implication, it exists.' An inference drawn from an exclusion.

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is not commanding us to set up the second pile. The proof comes from the exclusion: saying 'not on the other one' only makes sense if the other one is already there.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the priest shall burn wood upon it
every morning."
"Upon it," and not upon its companion.
This implies that its companion already exists.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וּבִעֵר עָלֶיהָ הַכֹּהֵן עֵצִים בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exclusion 'עליה ולא על חברתה' assumes the second pile is already on the מזבח when the logs are added, so the second pile comes first.

steps.title: The word 'upon it' is already used for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the word 'עליה' is needed to teach the basic מצוה of placing the logs. So it cannot also teach the order.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this word 'עליה' (upon it) is needed for its own basic meaning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source it just gave in Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16, the word 'עליה' was used to show that the other pile is already there when the logs are added. The objection is that this word is needed for its simple meaning: the כהן must put the wood on the מזבח. A word that is already busy teaching one thing usually cannot also teach a second thing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for
For its own basic meaning

phrases.english: But this word 'upon it'
is needed for its own basic meaning!
phrases.notes: It teaches the basic מצוה of placing wood on the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source drawn from the word 'עליה' in Step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is already used to teach the basic מצוה, so it is not free to teach the order.

steps.title: The word 'upon it' appears twice
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'עליה' two times. One teaches the basic מצוה, and the other teaches the order.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two 'עליה's are written in the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing out that the פסוק uses the word twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reads: 'the כהן shall burn wood עליה... and arrange the עולה עליה.' One 'עליה' gives the basic מצוה of putting wood on the מזבח. The extra 'עליה' is free to teach that the other pile is already there.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
Are written

phrases.english: Two 'upon it's are written.
phrases.notes: One for the basic מצוה, one for the order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is only one 'עליה', and it is used for the basic מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two, so one teaches the basic מצוה and the other teaches the order.
steps.whatToRemember: The source for the order of the logs stands, because the פסוק has two 'עליה's.

steps.title: The two logs come before cleaning the inner altar
steps.stepSummary: Next in אביי's list: the two logs are added before cleaning the מזבח הפנימי. Both have 'בבקר בבקר', but the act that makes something possible comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Adding the two logs comes before cleaning the inner altar. Both places in the תורה say 'every morning.' Even so, the act that makes another עבודה possible comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next item in אביי's list and gives its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the logs and the cleaning of the מזבח הפנימי are described with 'בבקר בבקר', so the פסוק does not tell us which comes first. The tie-breaker is that a מכשיר comes first. Wood makes it possible to bring coals for the קטורת, and the קטורת is burned on the מזבח הפנימי.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing the two logs of wood
Clearing ashes off the inner (golden) altar
Every morning
The act that makes something possible comes first

phrases.english: Placing the two logs of wood
comes before clearing the ashes of the inner altar.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּהָכָא כְּתִיב ״בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר״,
phrases.english: Even though here it is written 'every morning,'
phrases.notes: This 'every morning' is talking about the wood.

phrases.english: and here it is written 'every morning,'
phrases.notes: This 'every morning' is about the קטורת and the מזבח הפנימי, in שמות ל:ז.

phrases.english: even so, the act that makes things possible comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִידּוּר שְׁנֵי גְּזִירֵי עֵצִים קוֹדֵם לְדִישּׁוּן מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next link in אביי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two logs come before cleaning the מזבח הפנימי, because a מכשיר comes first.

steps.title: The two logs do not help the incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the two logs go on the big pile, not on the pile used for the קטורת coals. So how do they make the קטורת possible?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'making-possible' act? It is the two logs. But you said the two logs go to the big pile!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason 'מכשיר עדיף' from Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coals for the קטורת come from the second pile (מערכה שניה). The two logs are added to the מערכה גדולה. So they do not seem to help the קטורת at all, and the reason 'מכשיר' seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it?
But didn't you say?
The big pile of wood on the outer מזבח

phrases.english: What is the act that makes it possible?
The two logs of wood.
But didn't you say the two logs of wood
go to the big pile!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the two logs are a מכשיר for the קטורת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קטורת coals come from the second pile, but the logs go on the big pile, so they do not help the קטורת.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different piles. The big pile is for the קרבנות. The second pile is the source of coals for the קטורת. The two logs go on the big one.

steps.title: Wood in general makes the incense possible
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the logs belong to the category 'wood', and wood makes the קטורת possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is the category of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives the first answer to the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These particular logs do not feed the קטורת. But wood as a type is what makes the קטורת possible. Since the logs are wood, they get the priority of a מכשיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The category or 'name' of wood

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is the category of wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the exact wood used for the קטורת counts as a מכשיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Anything in the category of wood counts as a מכשיר.

steps.title: Once he started the piles, he finishes
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that since the כהן already started working on the wood piles, he finishes by adding the logs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Since he began with the pile, he finishes it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a second, different answer to the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא does not use the idea of מכשיר at all. The כהן was already building the piles, so he completes that whole job, including the two logs, before he moves to the מזבח הפנימי.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he began
He finishes

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Since he began with the pile, he finishes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: הוֹאִיל וְהִתְחִיל בַּמַּעֲרָכָה, גּוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason: finish a job you started
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The logs come first only if they are a מכשיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: They come first because they complete a job that was already started.

steps.title: Sometimes the big pile does supply the coals
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that if there is no wood for the second pile, coals are taken from the big pile. So the logs can make the קטורת possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If he does not find wood for the second pile, doesn't he bring coals in from the big pile?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third answer to the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same fact we saw in Step 14. When the second pile has no wood, the coals for the קטורת come from the big pile. So the logs on the big pile can sometimes really be a מכשיר for the קטורת.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not find
The second pile, the source of קטורת coals
He brings inside

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא מַשְׁכַּח עֵצִים לְמַעֲרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה
phrases.english: If he does not find wood for the second pile,
doesn't he bring coals in from the big pile?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אִי לָא מַשְׁכַּח עֵצִים לְמַעֲרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to Step 20, using the same fact as Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a real case where the logs are a מכשיר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The big pile never helps the קטורת.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the second pile has no wood, the big pile supplies the coals, so its logs can be a מכשיר.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers explain why the two logs come first: wood in general is a מכשיר (רבי ירמיה), you finish what you started (רבינא), and the big pile sometimes supplies the coals (רב אשי).

steps.title: Cleaning the inner altar comes before cleaning five lamps
steps.stepSummary: Next in אביי's list: cleaning the מזבח הפנימי comes before cleaning five of the lamps of the מנורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And cleaning the inner altar comes before cleaning five lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the next item in אביי's list. This sets up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הטבת נרות means cleaning and fixing the lamps of the מנורה. It was split into two parts: five lamps at one time and two lamps later. This rule places the cleaning of the מזבח הפנימי before the first five.

keyTerms.meaning: Cleaning and preparing the lamps of the מנורה
Five of the seven lamps

phrases.english: And clearing the ashes of the inner altar
comes before cleaning five lamps.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִישּׁוּן מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי קוֹדֵם לַהֲטָבַת חָמֵשׁ נֵרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next link in אביי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cleaning the מזבח הפנימי comes before cleaning five lamps of the מנורה.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why cleaning the מזבח הפנימי comes before the lamps.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule in Step 24. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no פסוק or מכשיר logic is given yet. So the גמרא wants to know what decides this order.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does cleaning the מזבח הפנימי come before cleaning the lamps?

steps.title: אביי: I know it by tradition only
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he received this rule as a tradition but does not know its reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I learned it as a tradition, but the reason I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the rule is a received tradition and he does not know its logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is honest. The rule is reliable because it was passed down, even though he cannot explain why. This leaves room for someone else to give a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: I learned it as a received tradition
The logical reason
I do not know

phrases.english: Abaye said:
I learned it as a tradition;
the reason, I do not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a tradition with no known reason.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'גמרא' does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition that was passed down.

steps.title: רבא: we do not pass over a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the order with ריש לקיש's rule that we may not pass over a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: It follows ריש לקיש. For ריש לקיש said: We do not pass over מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives an actual reason for the order, based on a rule of ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is: when you come to a מצוה, do it, and do not skip it to reach a different one. The גמרא will soon explain how this fits the layout of the היכל: the כהן reaches the מזבח הפנימי first, so he may not walk past it to the מנורה. The text continues on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not pass over a מצוה to do another
Following ריש לקיש

phrases.english: And Rava said: It follows Reish Lakish.
For Reish Lakish said:
We do not pass over the מצוות,
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reason where אביי gave none.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The order follows the rule 'אין מעבירין על המצות'.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'אין מעבירין על המצות' is a general rule that is used across ש״ס and in practical הלכה, for example in the order of putting on טלית and תפילין.
